metadata.title: Results from TALIS 2024: French Community of Belgium

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 note reports descriptive, self-report survey results for lower secondary teachers and principals in the French Community of Belgium, based on the OECD TALIS 2024 Database tables. The note does not specify the exact sampling/replicate weight variables or whether complex survey weights were applied in the computations shown. Because the document is a results note rather than a microdata analysis paper, the appropriate weighting approach is the one used by the OECD TALIS 2024 production process for international comparability (including handling of non-response and sampling design). Users should therefore rely on the OECD TALIS 2024 database documentation for the exact weight variable(s) and replicate design used when reproducing the reported percentages and statistically significant differences.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive results note based on TALIS self-reports and does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. As a result, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported indicators. The note also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) for the underlying survey responses, so the missing-data strategy cannot be verified from the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note presents findings based on responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals in the French Community of Belgium. It comments only on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average and does not describe further analytic filtering (e.g., exclusions for item non-response) in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 results note summarizes self-reported information from lower secondary teachers and principals in the French Community of Belgium collected in 2024. It reports percentages for teacher background (e.g., age distribution, gender, non-teaching work experience), teaching for today’s world indicators (e.g., adaptation to cultural diversity), student diversity and special education needs contexts, social and emotional skills confidence, and technology use (including AI use and hybrid/online teaching). It also summarizes teachers’ learning opportunities (initial teacher education preparation, induction/mentoring, and professional learning participation and barriers), teacher leadership/autonomy, professional relationships (with colleagues, principals, students, and parents/guardians), status of the profession, employment terms, demands of teaching (stress sources and working hours), and professional outcomes (lesson aims, well-being, job satisfaction, and retention intentions). The note is explicitly limited to statistically significant differences or changes and cautions that TALIS relies on self-reports, so cross-country comparisons should be interpreted carefully.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical ML/predictive study: it is a descriptive OECD results note that reports survey percentages and statistically significant differences/changes from TALIS 2024 tables. Consequently, there is no student-level outcome modeling, no ML algorithm evaluation, and no reported predictive performance metrics to extract. The absence of sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data procedures, and weighting variable names reflects the document’s purpose (communication of results rather than methodological transparency for re-analysis).
